reference: Ground Elapsed Time (GET) as HH:MM:SS from liftoff, 1969-07-16 13:32:00 UTC
source_notes: Timestamps and alarm codes reconstructed from NASA transcripts, the Apollo 11 Lunar Surface Journal (ALSJ), and Don Eyles' account of the 1202/1201 program alarms.

events.note: PDI - Powered Descent Initiation, throttle down to auto guidance
Rendezvous radar switch left in AUTO/SLEW per abort contingency procedure; CDU feeds AGC with spurious counts
First 1202 EXECUTIVE OVERFLOW - NO CORE SETS alarm. Executive ran out of core sets for the job queue.
Software restart: AGC clears non-essential (phantom) jobs and tasks, restarts core landing jobs (P63) from checkpoint via BAILOUT/priority restart logic

events.speaker: CAPCOM
events.note: Roger... We're GO on that alarm (relayed after Steve Bales / Jack Garman confirmed 1202 is on the 'GO' list)
Approach phase begins, LPD (Landing Point Designator) active
Second 1202 alarm - same executive overflow cause, radar still in AUTO
Second automatic recovery; guidance and navigation state preserved
1201 alarm - NO VAC AREAS (executive found no available VAC work area, same overload family as 1202)

events.speaker: Aldrin
events.note: 1202 alarm reported again; Bales/Garman confirm GO
Manual takeover (ATT HOLD/RATE OF DESCENT) as Armstrong redesignates landing site past West Crater
Low-level fuel quantity light; ~90 seconds of fuel margin as Armstrong searches for clear landing spot
Touchdown - Sea of Tranquility. 'The Eagle has landed.'
